change.author: Alex van Andel

findings.title: import() inside an object literal still loads every app eagerly, and each rejection is unhandled until awaited
findings.body: Every `import("./x")` in the `appStore` literal runs when `index.ts` is evaluated, so all ~30 app packages are still loaded as soon as anything imports `@calcom/app-store`. The PR's "async import" gives no lazy loading, and callers now pay an `await` for nothing. If any one app's module fails to load, its promise rejects at startup with no handler. The error only surfaces if a caller awaits that key, and otherwise it is an unhandled rejection. For real lazy loading, make each entry a loader function (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call it at the use sites. If eager loading is intended, say so in a comment.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) means the surrounding try/catch no longer catches calendar/video delete failures
findings.body: The callback is now `async`, and `forEach` ignores the promises it returns. A rejection from `getCalendar` (it now does a dynamic import), from `deleteEvent`, or from `deleteMeeting` (which is now `async`) is an unhandled promise rejection and never reaches the enclosing `try/catch`. The handler can also move on, and return, before the deletions have run. The same pattern is in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125`. Replace it with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the `try`. Alternatively, use a `for...of` loop with `await`, as this PR already does in `handleCancelBooking.ts:480`.

findings.title: forEach(async) pushes into apiDeletes after awaits, so the later Promise.all can miss the deletions
findings.body: The async `forEach` callback now awaits `getCalendar` and then `deleteEvent` before calling `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)`. The loop itself returns immediately, and `apiDeletes` is consumed at `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652). The pushes happen after at least two async hops, so recurring-booking calendar deletes can be missed by the `Promise.all` and their errors are unhandled. The new `await getCalendar` widens a race that already existed because of the `await deleteEvent`. Collect the per-credential promises first and push them synchronously, or `await` the loop with `for...of`. The adjacent legacy branch was already converted to `for...of` in this PR.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar`, which is a hidden contract change
findings.body: `getCalendar` is async, so `calendar` in each returned item is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>`. `getConnectedCalendars` handles this (`await item.calendar`, line 48). The exported `getCalendarCredentials` type changed silently, and the callers in `viewer.tsx:340`, `viewer.tsx:415` and `apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts:83` only pass the result straight to `getConnectedCalendars`. A future consumer that reads `.calendar` synchronously will get a truthy Promise. Consider resolving it in `getCalendarCredentials` (make it async and use `Promise.all`), or drop `calendar` from the returned object. It is only used inside `getConnectedCalendars`, and that function could call `getCalendar(credential)` itself.

contracts.action: getCalendar becomes async (dynamic appStore import); all callers must await
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous sync getCalendar callers in CalendarManager, EventManager, handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, trpc bookings, vital and wipemycalother reschedule
contracts.before_after: Every call site found by grep now has `await`, except the one in getCalendarCredentials, where the Promise is stored and awaited later in getConnectedCalendars. Sequential awaits now run inside the legacy for-loop in handleCancelBooking.
contracts.visible_effect: Calendar creation, update and deletion behave the same where the call is awaited.
contracts.failure_mode: The forEach(async) call sites (the two reschedule files, trpc bookings, handleCancelBooking:460) lose try/catch coverage and the ordering that apiDeletes relies on. Reported as findings.

contracts.action: videoClient getVideoAdapters made async; deleteMeeting made async
contracts.before_after: All internal callers (createMeeting, updateMeeting, deleteMeeting, the Cal video helpers, getBusyVideoTimes) now await it. External callers of deleteMeeting already treated it as returning a Promise.
contracts.visible_effect: No behaviour change besides the added microtask hops.
contracts.failure_mode: deleteMeeting no longer throws synchronously. The fire-and-forget callers in the reschedule files now fail as unhandled rejections (see finding).

contracts.action: Payment apps are loaded with await appStore[...] in handlePayment, deletePayment, handleCancelBooking and trpc bookings
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous sync lookup in each of the four call sites
contracts.before_after: All four sites were converted, and each sits inside an async function. The unknown-key case still gives `undefined`, which is handled by the existing `paymentApp &&` guard.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed module import would reject inside these async handlers and surface as an error. Before, it would have thrown at module load.

summary: The change converts appStore to dynamic `import()` promises and adds `await` at every call site. It also fixes the legacy loop in handleCancelBooking. The main defects are `forEach(async ...)` sites, which this PR creates or leaves in place: the three reschedule paths (vital, wipemycalother, trpc bookings) lose their try/catch, and the recurring-cancel loop in handleCancelBooking races its `apiDeletes` push. The `import()` calls inside the object literal still load all apps eagerly. `getCalendarCredentials` now exposes a Promise-typed `calendar`, which only `getConnectedCalendars` knows how to handle.
